source.title: Wearable Accelerometer Foundation Models for Health via Knowledge Distillation
source.authors: Salar Abbaspourazad; Anshuman Mishra; Joseph Futoma; Andrew C. Miller; Ian Shapiro

page_placements.theme: Individual tasks and metrics can plateau or reverse with scale

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses scaling laws in the context of wearable biosignal models but does not test the listed language-model scaling claims or measure held-out pretraining loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a two-size PPG encoder ablation using downstream prediction errors, and mentions signs of overfitting. These results do not measure the power-law behavior or compute-optimal allocation named by the claim versions. Scaling-law results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is about cross-modal knowledge distillation from PPG to accelerometry encoders. It cites Kaplan et al. only to explain overfitting in a two-size PPG-MAE ablation (6.3M vs 12.7M). It fits no scaling law and reports no pretraining loss across scale. The model-compression sweep (800K–6.3M, Fig. 4) reports downstream probe errors for distilled students, not power-law behaviour. Neither tests any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors saw initial overfitting when growing PPG-MAE from 6.3M to 12.7M parameters (8 to 16 layers). They suggest that the benefits of scaling laws may require growing model and data together, and leave scaling-law study of biosignal encoders to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not fit scaling laws or use the original language-model scaling-law procedure; its size ablation compares two wearable-signal encoder sizes on downstream metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: Doubling PPG-MAE encoder depth (6.3M to 12.7M) left heart-rate MAE unchanged (0.34) and raised SDNN and RMSSD MAE (4.46 to 5.05; 6.34 to 7.52). The authors call this initial overfitting at fixed data size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a wearable PPG masked-autoencoder setting with fixed data, increasing encoder size alone did not improve downstream probe error.

fits_no_version.finding: In the distillation compression sweep (students of 800K to 6.3M parameters, Fig. 4), downstream performance is largely maintained as size shrinks. Values are shown only in a figure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distilled accelerometry student encoders retain downstream performance across a roughly 5x range of size reduction.

record.problems: The scaling-related ablation compares only two encoder sizes and reports downstream prediction errors rather than held-out pretraining loss; no uncertainty estimates are given for these ablation values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-related results left out. Other scaling-law statements are citations or suggestions for future work, not results of this study.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss vs parameters, data or compute.
Shape effects at fixed parameter count on loss.
Power-law form in biosignal pretraining; only two sizes were compared, on downstream metrics.
Downstream predictability with scale. No trend was fitted; only two teacher sizes and a five-size student compression sweep were reported.

record.verdict_notes: The relation should be cites_only rather than discusses: Kaplan et al. is invoked only as a possible explanation in an appendix ablation. The paper's main topic is knowledge distillation, unrelated to scaling laws.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Effects of depth, width, and architecture at fixed parameter count on held-out pretraining loss.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the reported ablation does not measure pretraining-loss scaling.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

relation.reason: Appendix A.3 interprets the larger encoder's deterioration through scaling laws, suggests jointly increasing model and data size, and proposes future investigation. This goes beyond citation alone.

tranche.reason: The study reports distillation and model-size ablations, without fitting or evaluating a scaling law, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or downstream predictability. Scaling-law investigation is left to future work.

source_check.notes: The overfitting interpretation matches the authors' wording; joint model/data scaling is a proposed explanation, not a tested result. The supplied text is v2 dated 31 January 2025; the six rows represent three distinct comparisons.
